mechanism_narrative: Four consecutive weekly improvements in RETAIL_REC (from -9.7 to -4.9 percent below baseline) establish an autoregressive momentum that carries forward, so the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its trailing 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved in three of the last four weekly means
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days after four weeks of monotone improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility is the leading indicator of discretionary trip-making; once TRANSIT posts repeated week-on-week gains it pulls commuter and shopper footfall into retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT posts a week-on-week gain of at least 1.5 points in two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -51.4 to -46.3 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT gains at least 1.5 points twice in a row, the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC falls below its trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Falling RESIDENTIAL time-above-baseline means households are reallocating hours away from home; jointly with rising RETAIL_REC this substitution accelerates, and the interaction predicts further retail gains over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +5.0 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 6.0 to 4.1 while RETAIL_REC rose
regime_hint: post-lockdown normalization of household time use
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is below its trailing-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL continues to fall below +5.0 percent above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Recovery in PARKS mobility signals that residents have resumed voluntary out-of-home activity; this general outdoor normalization spills over into adjacent retail strips within roughly two weeks even without policy change.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -19.9 at t-1w to -14.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS posts a 3-point or larger week-on-week gain yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under a stage-based easing regime, workplace and transit mobility rise together because restrictions no longer cap movement; the resulting commuting volume mechanically restores weekday retail footfall over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -18.9 to -14.7 and TRANSIT from -51.4 to -46.3
failure_condition: Under a stage-based easing regime with both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improving, RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is below its trailing-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM above baseline reflects precautionary restocking and health-anxiety trips that substitute for discretionary outings; when this series exceeds +7 percent it crowds out retail-and-recreation visits in the following week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays above +7.0 for a week yet the subsequent weekly RETAIL_REC mean rises rather than falls.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of recovering WORKPLACES and TRANSIT is multiplicative: simultaneous gains mean both the commuter base and the trip capacity are restored, producing a larger retail uplift over four weeks than either series alone would imply.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved in the final two weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve, RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is no higher than in weeks where only one of them improves.

mechanism_narrative: Late-winter into early-spring daylight lengthening raises outdoor leisure trips, and PARKS gains lead retail-and-recreation gains by about two weeks as warmer-weather shopping and dining patterns resume.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and RETAIL_REC both improved in the final weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below its trailing-28-day mean while PARKS remains above its four-week average.
